questions.2.stimulus.title.back: A made-up object: the wooden spoon of Tavi village

questions.2.stimulus.items.1.source: One end is dark and burned.

questions.3.question.note: 'Nhìn gần' / 'nhìn rộng' for 'close view' / 'wide view' (zoom lesson). Must match the words used in the Vietnamese Lesson 3; check 'che khuất' is not too hard.

questions.3.question.back: Looking closely at the past shows what that looking widely can hide?

questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Growing over 100 years is a pattern. The wide view shows patterns very clearly. Look at Lesson 3 again.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: Who told this account, and why?
questions.4.options.2.text.back: Who told this account, and why?

questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. A historian asks who told an account, when and why. Each kind of question needs its own kind of answer.

questions.5.question.note: The young person is 'cô ấy' (she) as in the English; 'người trẻ' avoids confusion with 'bạn' (you). 'Học hỏi tập thể' for 'collective learning' is my own term, not in KEY_TERMS: native speaker please decide (alternatives: 'học hỏi chung', 'cùng học hỏi').
questions.5.question.source: A young person learns a skill from an older person. She makes it better. Then she teaches it to her friends. What is this called?
questions.5.question.back: A young person learns a skill from an older person. She makes it better. Then she teaches it to her friends. What is this called?

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. In collective learning, people share what they know, make it better and pass it on. This is how knowledge grows.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. In collective learning, people share what they know, make it better and pass it on. Knowledge grows this way.

questions.5.options.1.text.note: 'Trao đổi' for 'trade' here (the general idea); KEY_TERMS has 'buôn bán / trao đổi'. Check consistency with Lessons 6 and 8.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Trade means you give something and get something back. Here, a skill is shared and made better. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Exchange is when you give a thing and get a thing back. Here, a skill is shared and made better. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.5.options.2.text.note: 'Hái lượm' for 'foraging': my choice, not in KEY_TERMS. Check.

questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Gathering means finding food that grows wild. This example is about sharing a skill and making it better. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.6.question.note: 'Nhà khảo cổ' for archaeologist. 'Bếp lửa' for 'hearth': check it is clear (bếp lửa vs bếp). 'Nơi con người sinh sống thuở xa xưa' for 'early human sites' is a paraphrase.
questions.6.question.source: Archaeologists found these clues at early human sites. Which clue could show what people cooked?
questions.6.question.back: Archaeologists find these clues where people lived long ago. Which clue could tell what people cooked?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: The handprints on a rock wall

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Handprints are a kind of art. They tell us other things, not what people cooked. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Handprints are a form of art. They tell other things, not what people cooked. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: The hearth with its burned seeds

questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. A fireplace is where people lit fires. Burnt seeds in a fireplace could tell what people cooked.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: Tools of the same shape, far apart
questions.6.options.2.text.back: Tools of the same shape in places far apart

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. These tools may show that people shared ideas. They do not show what people cooked. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. These tools could show that people shared ideas. They do not tell what people cooked. Look at Lesson 5 again.
